doc.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Growing up in Southern California's traditional jazz scene
summary: Barrett was born in Pasadena, raised in Costa Mesa, and grew up around Sunday-afternoon Jazz Society meetings; he has played this festival three times.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well actually I was born in this area, I’m originally from Southern California. I was born in Pasadena. I was about one year old when my parents moved to Costa Mesa in Orange County, and I grew up in the more traditional jazz scene, the Sunday afternoon Jazz Society meetings that are still held around Southern California, which is as much a social event for people as a musical event. The fellows we call “weekend warriors” will get out their horns and, you know, dust off their basses and that kind of thing, and have a good time playing the old Dixieland warhorses at these Sunday afternoon Jazz Society meetings. So that’s what first got me interested in playing jazz, and that, I guess, accounts for why I’ve been invited to this festival. I think this is the third time I’ve done this now. I was here in 1987, then I had a few years off, and I was here last year and again this year.
